\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نفس} \fa{کشیدن} (nafas keshidan)}{نفس کشیدن (nafas keshidan)}]{\fa{نفس} \fa{کشیدن} (nafas keshidan) — to breathe}

\label{lesson:FA-C181-nafas-keshidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fry, then the Persian for to chop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نفس} \fa{کشیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{نفس} \fa{کشیدن}} — \emph{nafas keshidan} — \textquotedblleft{}to breathe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nafas keshidan} is \textquotedblleft{}to draw breath\textquotedblright{}: \emph{nafas} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{nafas}, \textquotedblleft{}breath\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; root \emph{n-f-s}, Lane), and \emph{keshidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw\textquotedblright{}, is native. \emph{keshidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{kašīdan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\emph{tekân dâdan} pairs \emph{tekân}, \textquotedblleft{}a shake\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}. \emph{tekân} is native Persian, but its older form is not settled. \emph{dâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*deh\textsubscript{3}-}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
